note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Defining and measuring DREs, then using a critic to mitigate them

nodes.name: DREs defined
nodes.description: Data referencing errors (DREs) are failures to faithfully locate and cite information from the input; for tables they split into Incorrect Citation (wrong values, confused rows/columns, fabricated content) and Omitted Information (missing required rows/values).

nodes.name: Dense tables invite DREs
nodes.description: Tables contain many similar rows and columns, which makes models prone to referencing the wrong data even when they parse the table structure correctly.

nodes.name: Judge with ground truth
nodes.description: A Sonnet-3.7 LLM-as-a-Judge that sees the ground-truth answer and judges response segments split at reflection tokens like 'Wait' detects DREs with 92.67% accuracy on manual inspection.

nodes.name: DREs are ubiquitous
nodes.description: DREs occur across models from 1.7B to 20B, across table formats (JSON, CSV, Markdown) and across tasks (QA, claim verification, table-to-text); e.g. Llama4-Scout has a 46.48% DRE rate on WTQ.

nodes.name: Reasoning and prompting do not remove DREs
nodes.description: Reasoning models with self-reflection still show DRE rates of 5.71%-46.04% on WTQ, and prompting Qwen3-8B to cite accurately leaves a 12.50% DRE rate and does not improve accuracy.

nodes.name: DREs correlate with wrong answers
nodes.description: Incorrect responses contain DREs far more often than overall (e.g. DRE-in-Incorrect 46.89% vs 14.04% DRE rate for Qwen3-8B on WTQ), yet many correct answers also contain DREs, so accuracy alone misses them.

nodes.name: Critic-based filtering helps
nodes.description: Selecting sampled responses with minimal DREs using the critic beats the average accuracy of all samples, and majority voting on the critic-filtered subset beats majority voting alone.

nodes.name: Rejection sampling with critic
nodes.description: Segment-level rejection sampling, resampling a segment until the critic accepts it (max 8 retries), improves accuracy by up to 11.96% without changing the generator.

nodes.name: DREs are avoidable
nodes.description: DREs are largely avoidable rather than fundamental limitations, since a DRE-free response can often be obtained simply by resampling.

nodes.name: Critic-4B is trained
nodes.description: A lightweight Qwen3-4B-Instruct critic is trained with SFT warm-up followed by RLVR on Qwen3-8B responses from the WTQ training set.

nodes.name: Critic-4B detects DREs well
nodes.description: Critic-4B reaches 78.16% overall F1 versus 69.51% for untrained Qwen3-4B-Instruct, generalizing to other datasets (TableBench, FinQA) and other models.

nodes.name: Critic-4B reduces DREs in inference
nodes.description: Rejection sampling with Critic-4B consistently raises accuracy and lowers DRE rate for larger generators, though less than the stronger Sonnet-3.7+gt critic.

isolated_nodes.name: Synthetic-data critic overfits
isolated_nodes.description: Critic-4B-Synthetic, trained on synthetic data, improves in-distribution but declines on FinQA and Llama4-Scout, suggesting overfitting to synthetic biases.

isolated_nodes.name: Scale helps within a family
isolated_nodes.description: Within the Qwen3 family, larger models produce fewer DREs, but this trend does not hold across model families.

isolated_nodes.name: Errors repeat once made
isolated_nodes.description: Once a reasoning model makes a first DRE it often repeats it, relying more on its own generation than on the original table.

structural_reasoning: Definition and judge underpin the prevalence findings; the measured link between DREs and wrong answers motivates critic filtering and rejection sampling; the trained small critic feeds the cheaper rejection sampling.
